title: Network evidence pipeline design and hardening checklist for private deployments
content:
Purpose and scope:

This working doc describes an end-to-end design for collecting, protecting, and exporting network-related evidence from Redwood Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) into a centralized SIEM and evidence store for compliance audits. Focus areas: RBAC v2 mapping for audit enrichment, an audit log schema for network events, SIEM ingestion patterns, evidence bundle automation, VPC/firewall patterns, mTLS expectations for service-to-service traffic, and a practical hardening checklist for operator runbooks.

Audience and assumptions:
- Audience: platform engineers, SREs, security engineers, and professional services engineers running private deployments.
- Assumptions: customer private deployment includes a control plane (managed or self-hosted), one or more inference clusters, and a transit VPC or peering to customer VPC(s). Logs can be forwarded via syslog/TCP/TLS or HTTPS and can be stored in a customer-managed S3-compatible store or pushed to a SIEM endpoint.

High-level flow (textual diagram):

  [Control Plane] --mTLS--> [Dedicated Inference Nodes / Pool] 
         |                              |
         | syslog/HTTPS (signed)        | local audit + network logs
         v                              v
  [Log Forwarder / Fluent-bit] --> [Edge Log Aggregator (TLS + signing)] --> [SIEM / Evidence S3]

Key design points:
1) Single canonical audit log schema (network-focused)
- Use a flat key namespace so fields are easily mapped in SIEM. Fields below are required for each network/audit event: timestamp, tenant_id, deployment_id, host_id, service_name, src_ip, src_port, dst_ip, dst_port, proto, action (ALLOW/DENY), rule_id, conn_id, bytes_in, bytes_out, tls (boolean), tls_cipher, client_cert_subject, server_cert_subject, principal (rbac principal id), request_id, trace_id, outcome, raw_message_hash.
- Example log line (JSON single-line):
  {"timestamp":"2025-02-02T12:11:03Z","tenant_id":"tenant-42","deployment_id":"dep-a1","host_id":"i-0a1b2c3d4e","service_name":"inference-worker","src_ip":"10.1.5.10","src_port":52342,"dst_ip":"10.2.10.4","dst_port":443,"proto":"TCP","action":"DENY","rule_id":"fw-eu-003","conn_id":"cdb3b6","bytes_in":0,"bytes_out":0,"tls":true,"tls_cipher":"TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256","client_cert_subject":"CN=svc-agent,OU=rlw","server_cert_subject":"CN=control-plane","principal":"svc-account:projectX:role-audit-reader","request_id":"req-9a8b7","trace_id":"trace-99","outcome":"blocked","raw_message_hash":"sha256:..."}

2) RBAC v2 mapping for audit enrichment
- Every service account and human user used in private deployments must map to a stable principal string (e.g., svc-account:team:role or user:email).
- Ensure every request that affects network state (e.g., firewall change, route add, peering creation) emits an "actor" field that includes principal, role, and source_identity (IP/instance).
- Maintain a lightweight roles manifest (YAML/CSV) per-deployment stored with the evidence store so auditors can map role IDs to permissions at the time of the event.

3) SIEM ingestion patterns and backpressure handling
- Primary ingestion: TLS-encrypted HTTP(s) endpoint with mutual auth preferred for push (recommended). Secondary: syslog over TLS to a collector.
- Logs should be batched and compressed (gzip) with max batch size 1MB and max interval 10s to reduce overhead without losing timeliness.
- Forwarders must support at-least-once delivery. To avoid duplicate counting in compliance reports, include raw_message_hash and sequence numbers. SIEM parsers should deduplicate on raw_message_hash + tenant_id + timestamp window.

4) Evidence automation and integrity guarantees
- Evidence bundle per audit window (daily or per-retention policy) containing: flattened logs, roles-manifest.json, snapshot of active firewall rules (read-only), snapshot of network ACLs and route tables, certificate inventory (serial + subject + valid_from + valid_to), and a signed manifest (manifest.json) with a bundle_hash and signer metadata.
- Signing: use KMS/HSM to produce an attestation signature for the manifest. Include signing key id and certificate chain in bundle metadata.
- Storage: evidence bundles written to customer-provided S3 path with object ACLs restricted; apply server-side encryption and bucket policies that enforce MFA-delete if available.

5) VPC and firewall patterns (recommended baseline)
- Topology pattern: transit VPC controls shared services + NAT + egress filtering. Customer VPCs peer to transit VPC using VPC peering or transit gateway.
- Firewall posture: default deny inbound to control plane endpoints; allow only specific management CIDRs (SRE office VPN ranges, customer on-prem mgmt proxies).
- Egress: avoid open 0.0.0.0/0 egress for worker nodes. Use enterprise NAT + explicit allow lists for external dependencies (model registry, telemetry endpoints).
- Healthchecks: open only the minimal healthcheck ports between load balancers and nodes; put healthcheck IP ranges in rule comments and snapshots to aid audits.

6) mTLS requirements and cert lifecycle
- All internal RPCs between control-plane and inference nodes must use mutual TLS with short-lived certs (recommended TTL <= 24h). Use an automated issuer (ACME-like or internal CA) with automated rotation and revocation lists pushed to nodes.
- Certificates must include instance identity metadata in SANs (tenant_id, deployment_id, instance_id). Forwarding proxies (log forwarders) should capture client_cert_subject and server_cert_subject in logs.

7) Minimal audit readiness checklist (operator-friendly)
- Logging and collection:
  - [ ] Fluent-bit/forwarder configured to sign and forward network/audit logs to aggregator endpoint over TLS.
  - [ ] Forwarder uses sequence numbers and raw_message_hash for dedupe.
  - [ ] Syslog/HTTPS endpoints validated by SIEM team (test vector pass).
- RBAC & roles:
  - [ ] Roles manifest present in evidence bucket for current retention window.
  - [ ] Every human and service principal mapped and exported to manifest (include creation_time and owner).
- Firewall and VPC snapshots:
  - [ ] Daily snapshot job runs and stores firewall rules and route tables in evidence store (immutable).
  - [ ] Rule_list includes rule_id, created_by, last_modified_by, and last_modified_ts.
- mTLS and certs:
  - [ ] Certificate inventory exported daily; expiry alerts configured for <= 7 days.
  - [ ] Automated rotation tested in staging monthly.
- Evidence bundles and signing:
  - [ ] Evidence bundle creation job runs daily (or per policy) and produces a signed manifest.
  - [ ] Signing key rotation policy documented and tested.
- SIEM and retention:
  - [ ] SIEM ingestion configured; test alerts generated for a sample deny event.
  - [ ] Retention policy validated (logs retained at least X days per compliance requirement).

8) Example operational runbook (short)
- Scenario: Auditor requests firewall evidence for 2025-01-20 to 2025-01-22 for tenant-42.
  1. Run artifact exporter: select tenant_id=tenant-42 and date range -> pulls signed evidence bundles from S3.
  2. Verify manifest signature using KMS public key.
  3. Open firewall snapshot file; filter for rule_ids referenced in SIEM deny events.
  4. Produce a short CSV with (timestamp,event_id,rule_id,outcome,actor) for the auditor.

9) Minimal tech debt and future work (notes)
- Improve schema versioning: include schema_version in every log to allow SIEM pipelines to handle evolution.
- Add canonical network topology spec (YAML) that can be validated by CI during deployment.
- Integrate with centralized policy engine for rule drift detection and auto-remediation suggestions.

Action items (owners):
- Ethan: prototype signed evidence bundle producer (end-to-end) by 2025-02-16.
- Priya: add RBAC principal export to roles manifest generator by 2025-02-09.
- Marco: run SIEM ingestion tests and create test vectors by 2025-02-12.

Notes and open questions:
- Should the evidence bundle include full packet captures for high-severity incidents? (pros: forensics; cons: PII and storage)
- How to coordinate cross-tenant dedupe when tenants share a transit VPC? Proposed: include tenant_id and conn_id in dedupe key at SIEM.

End of doc.
